title: Timers
objective: Schedule work with setTimeout, setInterval and clearInterval, and avoid overlapping timers
story: In the Event Belt, time is an event too: a tick every second! Today you'll build countdowns, clocks and stopwatches with **timers**.

tasks.title: Delayed launch
tasks.prompt:
When the `#launch` button is clicked:

- `#info` immediately becomes `Getting ready...`,
- and **200 ms later** (`setTimeout`) it becomes `Liftoff!`.
tasks.starter:
const info = document.querySelector("#info");

// listen to the click event and use setTimeout inside it
hints: Write the first text right away, outside setTimeout.

tasks.title: Flight time
tasks.prompt:
When the page opens, `count` goes up by 1 every **100 ms** and shows in `#count` (`setInterval`).

When the `#stop` button is clicked, the timer stops (`clearInterval`).

tasks.title: Blinking light
tasks.prompt:
The signal light `#light` blinks every **100 ms**: toggle the `on` class (`classList.toggle`) and add 1 to `blinks`.

After 6 changes (`blinks === 6`) the timer stops. `#blinks` shows the number of changes.

challenge.title: Stopwatch
challenge.prompt:
Build a stopwatch. `tenths` counts tenths of a second; `#watch` shows it like `2.3` (`(tenths / 10).toFixed(1)`).

- `#start`: starts adding to `tenths` every 100 ms. If it's **already running**, it must not start a new timer!
- `#stop`: stops the timer (`timer` becomes `null` again so it can be restarted).
- `#reset`: stops it, sets `tenths` to 0 and shows `0.0`.
hints: if (timer !== null) return; stops it starting twice.

project_task.title: Countdown timer
project_task.prompt:
The game should last 10 seconds. Write two functions:

- `tick()`: takes 1 from `timeLeft` (never below 0) and writes it into `#time`. When it reaches 0, it stops the timer (`clearInterval`) and writes `Time's up!` into `#info`.
- `startTimer()`: first stops the old timer, sets `timeLeft` to 10 and writes it into `#time`, then starts the timer with `setInterval(tick, TICK_MS)`.

`startTimer()` is already called when the form is submitted. To make it easy to test, `TICK_MS` is 100 ms for now; in the real game you'd use 1000.
